[b]Intro[/b]
There is no doubt that the reunification of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur in the late summer of 2028 led to a massive societal upheaval, splitting history into a pre-union and a post-union world.

Where the pre-union world was driven by the raving madness of the socialist experiments of the mid-2020s, the post-union world came to be a restoration of the classical model of life, at least for the government of the newly created Grande Montfleur.

The people of both countries, however, viewed matters differently. In early September, the triumphant revolution had come to a close, and the citizens of both nations were left with a system that seemed all so foreign to them. Montfleur was used to a quiet and non-aligned life, Rosenmarkke was used to the cosmopolitan technocratic system which had led to rapid growth and rapid centralization. However, the temporary decentralisation of the territories formerly known as Rosenmarkke under the August 11th treaty left many regions which had once seen themselves as brothers of their neighbors questioning and wondering what the hell they were to do.

It was easier for regions like Knygta and Deyn, and Thýven, which had always been bastions of local culture, Belgarde had always leaned towards Montfleurois. However, for Mittlemarkke and Westmarkke, these had shaped the cosmopolitan center of Rosenmarkke and as such were for all intents and purposes, Rosenmarkket but, if the nation existed no longer, what were they? 

Rolfe Rike in The Progression of History, a story of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur, published in 2029.

[b]September 5, 2028: Imperial Ambitions[/b]
Have you heard the rumors out of Valcouerghastly little things these are, but the king intends to declare himself Emperor, stated the voice of one Anna Paolina of Thýven, her petite form wrapped in the most elegant of Montfleurois fashion, her hair pinned back by a diamond family heirloom hairpin.

Of what? Surely he wouldnt claim the East, it would disrupt our neighbors, laughed Colonel Ernst Ralouette, a noble from Montfleur who had become acquainted with Anna Paolina through the various public circles that had formed in the aftermath of the reunification a month earlier. 

I do wonder what these rumors mean, intoned Thomas Lambeau, one of the famed members of the International Association for the Reunification of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur, and the writer of the Declaration of Grievances that had led to the formal reunification.

Well it makes one wonder if re-unifcation was ever a good thing, if we are to be handed from one despot to the next, exclaimed Anna, with a sip of cognac as the swirling ballroom music made its way across the room.

Anna had always been a socialite among the Thývenic society; however, recent years had led to a more austere lifestyle, which she had begrudgingly felt compelled to adopt to ensure she served in the suffering of her fellow citizens. Now, however, that the government had gone away and the future seemed brighter, she had brought out the finery once again. This was the first of many balls she had planned to host, all done up in the old style of the ancien regime to honour the new Montfleurois patrons of the Rosenmarkket region. 

Oh of course not, I am good friends with the king, if Henri tries any funny business, the duchess of Lorrainewho by the way, may I remind you is the actual head of government, will beat him to shape, replied Lambeau. 

Oh, Eleonore, isnt she such a wonderful woman! declared Anna, I would wonder why she isnt queen instead of Henri, 

They did date, it was rumored as a possibility, replied the colonel, leaning and rocking forward on his toes.

Ah, well, what a happy relationship that wouldve been, replied Anna, In fact, another thing I heard, and this from my friend in Valcouer, they are dating again, 

I wouldnt put it past those two, if not for love, but for stability, replied the colonel with a sly grin.

Speaking of love, have you seen the Colletes? I heard Mr. Collete had made love to a maid or some other household servant, said Anna.

Madame Paolina, I do not introduce myself to such hearsay, replied the Colonel, It is unbecoming. 

Oh well, it would be such a drag if the rumor was true, I mean, they are the patrons of the time, billions are coming from their pocket and into the regions most affected by the reunification, replied Anna. 

Oh I heard it was a male maid, shuddered Lambeau.

What?! Exclaimed Anna, I thought he was orthodox? Oh heavenswell, we shant have anymore of that talk, she waved her fan before her, before walking off to speak with the other guests. 

Lambeau looked at the colonel and shrugged, I assume everything is alright with the command? he asked.

Oh yes, General Martel has done a good job at re-organising the forces, replied the colonel.

Well, chortled Lambeau, At least he isnt sleeping with the male maids, 

The colonel laughed, Oh how droll Mr. Lambeau, and I thought you were more behaved than that! 

Lambeau nodded and then wandered the room to speak with the others, leaving the colonel in his uniform, standing in the corner, a glass of champagne in his hand.

The party continued into the night as the revelers made sure to make themselves known to the hostess, whose connections were of great renown. As the night drew to a close, that dainty hostess made her way into the drawing room with the few guests she had discreetly invited for them to meet her aging mother, who was rumored to be the grandest dame in Thýven.

Of course, Lambeau and the Colonel had been roped in, with Anna declaring proudly as she produced the two men, Now see here are the two heroes of this region.

To which Lambeau brushed off the compliment with a laugh, and the colonel merely smiled, he had grown tired and was ready to retire. Unfortunately, the cards had not his retirement from the fête that night, for the arrival of one Madame Eliza Collete (the eldest daughter of the estranged Mr. and Mrs. Collete). 

She was of fine form, draped in a simpler dress which fell to the floor like a pillar, her hair pinned up in pearls, and a set of matching earrings. Upon her arrival, many sought to avoid the scandalous young lady, who had only just been brought out into society the year prior upon her twenty-second birthday, which to many was later than usual. 

Anna, however, was not about to lose the tea of the evening, and as a result, despite the frownings of her mother, made haste to introduce the shy lady to the drawing room and its occupants. 

See here, the lady of the night, clapped Anna with delight, presenting the timid Eliza to her mother, who nodded with a frown.

See there, the shyest of the Colletes it seems, muttered Lambeau with a chuckle.

However, the colonel found himself peculiarly drawn to her, making towards her in the drawing room to provide her his seat, he bowed to her, and taking her hand led her to her seat, Good afternoon madame, he intoned politely, to which she merely smiled.

Is it so that you have drawn yourself to her? mused Anna out loud, moving her fan to cover her mouth.  How scandalous of you, Colonel, she said playfully, tapping his shoulder.

Oh but he doesnt draw himself to scandals madame Anna, declared Lambeau.

I have merely offered a seat, scoffed the colonel, with a pleading look at the whispering guests.

And they say chivalry is dead Anna, intoned the elderly mother with a laugh, The Montfleurois are the ones to bring it back, 

And it was in this manner that the rest of the night continued, silent conversation made between the guests as the band finally wound down, and Anna made haste to shoo those who were not directly within her circle out. 

However, the Colonel and Eliza found themselves out on the sidewalk before the townhouse, the nightlights of the city giving a glow upon their forms as the last of the guests' chauffeurs pulled away. 

Goodbye! cried Anna from the top step of the doorway.

To which the colonel merely nodded and proceeded to turn his attention to Eliza, Have you a car? he asked as she walked down the sidewalk.

No, I shall take the taxi, she replied coolly, her dress sweeping along the ground.

Oh I couldnt allow that, come back to Madame Paolinas house, replied the colonel.

My good sir, if it was my intent to stay at her house I wouldve enquired of her chauffeur, replied Eliza, turning away from the colonel as they stopped on the sidewalk.

Well perhaps you were too shy, replied the colonel.

Nosy is what you are, she replied sharply, beginning to walk again, Now do stop following me or I shall scream, 

The colonel stopped, As you wish, 

Eliza stopped once more, a few paces away, and turned to him, Are you so reluctant to let a lady into the night? she asked.

Well you asked for me to stop following you, scoffed the colonel.

Oh yes, replied Eliza with a wave of her hand, I did, but perhaps I have changed my mind,

The colonel frowned. She was playing a game, a game unbefitting of her, Now maam, let me hail you some more suitable ride, 

No need, replied Eliza, stepping off the curb and waving a taxi down. One noticed her and began to slow down.

Very well, have a good night, madame, replied the colonel as she opened the door and stepped in.

I shall, she replied, slamming the door shut and directing the driver to speed off, leaving the colonel standing on the quiet sidewalk, he stood there for a few minutes before nodding his head and walking off.

Mario was writing a letter to both Neue and Wuloosya in an aggressive manner. The Neue Letter was more friendly, but the Wuloosya one, not soo much...

"'and you are a big jerk', THERE! I'm done!" Mario shouted with relief as he threw his pen into the air, "Time to se-!"

"Mario! Don't scream when everyone is waking up! You ruined my dream!" Groaned Luigi, who was still wearing his pajamas and his pajama hat, "What are you doing anyway?"

Luigi then grabs the Neue Letter, and he liked it, "Hey! This one sounds pretty diplomatic and stuff! especially the 'We believe peace is the better option.' line!"

and then he looked at the Wuloosya letter, "Mario, is this a good idea to send this?"

"What's wrong?" Asked Mario.

"Mario, this sounds very harsh," replied Luigi.

"What? Luigi, do you think 10 days are enough to do all the stuff that was inside the Wuloosya Ultimatum?"

"No," Said Luigi.

"And look at the Negative effects the Ultimatum has caused! My people have lost trust in me because I was following the Ultimatum, more people became jobless, AND THERE ARE MORE EXTREMIST GROUPS!"

"And don't forget that they literally just say I'm doing nothing to fulfill the ultimatum, ONE DAY AFTER THEY GAVE ME THAT! An-"

"Mario, don't you think that their voting on April 21st was a voting to prepare, and the declaration thingy was made, maybe a few days ago? Not April 21st?" Luigi kindly interrupted Mario, "like you got the declaration a few days ago."

"Hey, that kinda makes sense, let me write a note on the bottom," said Mario.

"By the way, I got some news ab-" said Luigi, but was cut off by Mario.

"ABOUT MY DAUGHTER?!" Asked Mario frantically

"no"

"Anywho, I got some info about the April 12th incident," continued Luigi, "turns out, the reason the RISF used mustard gas happened because someone, when filling up tear gas, thought mustard gas smelled like mustard, like the one for hotdogs, and that said person hates mustard!"

"Luigi," said Mario, "that is the most stupid info I've heard, and I'm gonna put it inside the letter."

"Mario, I think I should fix your letter." "said Luigi, as He snatched the letter from Mario's hands, then he spedrun on fixing the stuff inside the letter, "done!"

"Ooh, let me see," Said Mario, "Luigi you just made this letter make me look weak, what do you mean by 'pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, pleas, don't invade us!'???"

"aw camon Mario, that would make our neighbours feel bad for us!"

"Let me revert it back."

[i]A few rewriting moments later...[/i]

"ok, ok compromise," said Luigi, whose hands are already tired, "I will edit it, but not massively edit it, ok, Mario?"

"There we go!"

[i]later...[/i]

"There, finished!" Said Luigi, after fixing some stuff on the letter, "Using the computer was much better than using paper!"

"ok! I'll send them!" said Mario in an unnecessarily cheerful way.

"Mario, if Wuloosya declares war after they receive the letter, don't get angry at me, especially since you don't want to be deported but Wuloosya wants you to be," said Luigi, "but at least the Neue Letter was ok and Nice."

"Bah," Said Mario, "anyways Who was the name of the soldier who hated mustard? We need to send him to the International Court of Justice and bla-bla-blah."

"Unfortunately, I donno." Replied Luigi in an unfortunate tone.

As the night drew to a close, that dainty hostess made her way into the drawing room with the few guests she had discreetly invited for them to meet her aging mother, who was rumored to be the grandest dame in Thýven.

Of course, Lambeau and the Colonel had been roped in, with Anna declaring proudly as she produced the two men, Now see here are the two heroes of this region.

To which Lambeau brushed off the compliment with a laugh, and the colonel merely smiled, he had grown tired and was ready to retire. Unfortunately, the cards had not his retirement from the fête that night, for the arrival of one Madame Eliza Collete (the eldest daughter of the estranged Mr. and Mrs. Collete). 

She was of fine form, draped in a simpler dress which fell to the floor like a pillar, her hair pinned up in pearls, and a set of matching earrings. Upon her arrival, many sought to avoid the scandalous young lady, who had only just been brought out into society the year prior upon her twenty-second birthday, which to many was later than usual. 

Anna, however, was not about to lose the tea of the evening, and as a result, despite the frownings of her mother, made haste to introduce the shy lady to the drawing room and its occupants. 

See here, the lady of the night, clapped Anna with delight, presenting the timid Eliza to her mother, who nodded with a frown.

See there, the shyest of the Colletes it seems, muttered Lambeau with a chuckle.

However, the colonel found himself peculiarly drawn to her, making towards her in the drawing room to provide her his seat, he bowed to her, and taking her hand led her to her seat, Good afternoon madame, he intoned politely, to which she merely smiled.

Is it so that you have drawn yourself to her? mused Anna out loud, moving her fan to cover her mouth.  How scandalous of you, Colonel, she said playfully, tapping his shoulder.

Oh but he doesnt draw himself to scandals madame Anna, declared Lambeau.

I have merely offered a seat, scoffed the colonel, with a pleading look at the whispering guests.

And they say chivalry is dead Anna, intoned the elderly mother with a laugh, The Montfleurois are the ones to bring it back, 

And it was in this manner that the rest of the night continued, silent conversation made between the guests as the band finally wound down, and Anna made haste to shoo those who were not directly within her circle out. 

However, the Colonel and Eliza found themselves out on the sidewalk before the townhouse, the nightlights of the city giving a glow upon their forms as the last of the guests' chauffeurs pulled away. 

Goodbye! cried Anna from the top step of the doorway.

To which the colonel merely nodded and proceeded to turn his attention to Eliza, Have you a car? he asked as she walked down the sidewalk.

No, I shall take the taxi, she replied coolly, her dress sweeping along the ground.

Oh I couldnt allow that, come back to Madame Paolinas house, replied the colonel.

My good sir, if it was my intent to stay at her house I wouldve enquired of her chauffeur, replied Eliza, turning away from the colonel as they stopped on the sidewalk.

Well perhaps you were too shy, replied the colonel.

Nosy is what you are, she replied sharply, beginning to walk again, Now do stop following me or I shall scream, 

The colonel stopped, As you wish, 

Eliza stopped once more, a few paces away, and turned to him, Are you so reluctant to let a lady into the night? she asked.

Well you asked for me to stop following you, scoffed the colonel.

Oh yes, replied Eliza with a wave of her hand, I did, but perhaps I have changed my mind,

The colonel frowned. She was playing a game, a game unbefitting of her, Now maam, let me hail you some more suitable ride, 

No need, replied Eliza, stepping off the curb and waving a taxi down. One noticed her and began to slow down.

Very well, have a good night, madame, replied the colonel as she opened the door and stepped in.

I shall, she replied, slamming the door shut and directing the driver to speed off, leaving the colonel standing on the quiet sidewalk, he stood there for a few minutes before nodding his head and walking off.

Krigleves, Hlagirhan, and Segvuvid
[spoiler]
The history of the Dunmer people (also known as dark elves or simply elves) within the reaches of Alaqar begins with the introduction of the Dunmer people into Alaqar 20,000 years ago. Humans were not present in Alaqar at this time, and as such the Dunmer were left to their own devices in the area. They were spread out across the nation of modern-Alaqar, however there is a strange lack of evidence of Dunmer settlement outside of Alaqars borders. There is no clear theory as to why this happened, however some suggest that Dunmer connections to ones ancestors caused limited movement due to the construction of ancestral graves and structures that kept settlements sedentary.

Dunmer influences in Alaqar were crippled by the arrival of modern Homo sapiens into the region, referred to more commonly as humans. The humans initially lived in relative peace with the Dunmeric peoples, as it was hard for either race to contract diseases or sicknesses from one another. However, this peace was not to last, as tribal feuds turned into full scale conflicts, the humans and Dunmer ended up fighting against one another over resources, land or simply over race. The humans were able to, albeit slowly, force the Dunmer across the Shaki Mountains, leading to the destruction of many Dunmer settlements west of the mountains. The humans were unable to launch a coherent attack against the Dunmer across the mountains, as the bitter rivalries between the clans sparked infighting once again.

Dunmer left on the west side were persecuted or forced to assimilate into the human culture. Most Dunmer on the west side either were exiled and forced to move east or moved on their own accord to the eastern lands. The Dunmer tribes that lived west were assimilated into families and tribes of the east, solidifying human expansion into western Alaqar. After the mass migration, Dunmer people formed settlements along the Gnar and Iccin Rivers, two very important rivers for transportation and agriculture across the Dunmer lands. They also were the base for many salt, silver and other mineral mining communities that contributed to Dunmer economies. The Gnar River specifically saw various settlements formed such as Sagol Sehn in the 800s BC and Dedroc in the 600s BC. Sagol Sehn, which roughly translates to Sehns Song, survived as a city up to the modern day and serves as the modern capital of Krigleves. The Iccin and Gnar River both funneled into Lake Iccinagihn, a lake that separates the modern states of Gnarisa and Hlagirhan.

Around the year 550 BCE, the Joran Empire rose beyond the Shaki Mountains. The Jorans composed of mainly Fezilik peoples and mainly kept their bounds in human lands. While the empire initially left the Dunmer alone, it would eventually make an attempt on the city states lined on the edge of the Dark Elf world. In 543 BCE, the city of Heydaxiar was besieged by the Joran Empire. Heydaxiar was a middling city state on the far west of the Dunmer realms, prized for its strategic location near the Shaki Mountains, defendable position and its economy in iron mining. When the Jorans arrived to Heydaxiar, the response was swift and brutal. Almost 2/3 of the Dunmer world sent troops or money to Heydaxiar to prevent the humans from entering Dunmer lands, and the Joran army was quickly outmatched. What was expected to be a long and lengthy siege turned into swift retreat, as the Jorans went from 30,000 men to merely 4,000. The Joran Empire retreated its army and would never attempt to enter Dark Elf lands for the rest of its existence. The Siege of Heydaxiar would mark the only major military confrontation between humans and Dunmer for 500 years.

It was also around this time of isolation from Alaqan powers that the Dunmer began splitting into their modern cultural bases. Cities like Heydaxiar, Knamaxid and Venro Vil were up to this point controlled by various city states and small, regional kingdoms. This era had lasted thousands of years before the Joran invasion, and left the lands constantly at odds with each other. This changed with the emergence of House Hlagir in the south. House Hlagir, which in 379 was headed by Gidaryn Hlagir, launched a bold military and political campaign on their neighboring city states. House Hlagir married off into the families of Krandoni and Zaydonmed, securing their respective territories into the personal union of Hlagir, the heart of the rising kingdom. Attacks were launched on lands or families that broke free of House Hlagirs influence. Hlagirhan was eventually formed from Gidaryns campaigns, and it became the dominant power for decades in the region. House Segvu and House Krig attempted to stretch their own power to challenge House Hlagir, and successfully expanded their political reach to match that of Hlagirhan. All three of these houses were in the far south of the Dunmer realms, and were distanced from the houses that bordered the Shaki Mountains more directly.

For centuries, the Dunmer world was a slow game of power between the various houses of the region, constantly challenging one anothers power and trying to undermine governments and families for their own benefit. However, they were able to repel human invasions from the west due to their own internal fighting, leaving the Dunmer to their own devices. Economically, this saw great results for common Dunmer peoples. Food and water was a non-issue thanks to the Iccin and Gnar Rivers, but the Dunmer mainly excelled at craftsmanship and innovation. Skilled Dunmer craftsmanship would build houses out of the inside of giant mushrooms, which served as the homestead of Dunmer royalty and could live for hundreds of years if properly maintained. Botanists, not just from Alaqar but from various Shamatine backgrounds, studied these illustrious plants while visiting Dunmer lands. As Ghijandi botanist Ruslan Latif put it, These mushrooms they almost dont follow the laws of nature. The medieval dark elves were able to grow their own houses, houses that reached dozens of feet into the air. To a human, with such a poor view on the Dunmer people at the time, seeing them build homes that they could only dream of making themselves was surreal. These mushroom houses became the cornerstone of Dunmer culture and seeds became luxuries for outside realms.

In 1267, the Convention of Sarytagan took place between the powers of Alaqar over in the west. Various kingdoms such as Yalakol, Terakhia and Nasiv as well as the city state of Shiganuur were established into a united Khaganate of Alaqar. House Hlagir, House Segvu and House Krig all sent diplomats to the capital of Alaqar, Shiganuur, to try and establish relations with the Khagan. While initially successful, the famed General Badai took control of the Alaqan Khaganate, installing his son on the throne and leaving to go on a military campaign across the Shaki Mountains. His son, Dadajon Badai, was a surprisingly reasonable and friendly man, and continued holding relations with the states not under attack by General Badais men out east. The northern Dunmer states were overrun by Badai, placed under the control of the Alaqan Khaganate and were forced to give resources to Shiganuur. Dunmer men were not forced to fight for Badais army, as Badai did not want to risk fighting potential revolts against trained Dunmer men with access to Alaqars logistics and military supplies. Krigleves, led by House Krig had run-ins with Alaqan divisions during Badais campaign, but both sides generall avoided conflicting with each other as Badai didnt want to advance south into hostile Dunmer territory.

After Badai died mid-campaign and Alaqar began declining, the Dunmer states saw a chance to liberate their people from human rule. Alaqar suffered from numerous wars with their smaller neighbors, wars which began to break apart the state. Riots were a common occurrence, instability was a constant problem and the Khaganates military forces, now comprised of mainly mercenary groups, were stretched to their absolute limits. Dunmer armies had no problems waltzing through Alaqars far eastern territories during the First Fracturing. For soldiers and fighters, this was one of the most brutal periods of pre-modern history to fight in. Ancient and medieval Alaqans had used hell hogs from the northern Qarikan Desert to great effect past the Shaki Mountains, using them as other cultures would use horses to wage an incredibly destructive style of warfare. Dunmer from the same area used guar, a creature native to the Dunmer lands that looked like a small dinosaur. Both guar and hell hogs often fought against one another in fierce, close-up battles, while their riders fought head to head with spears, axes, daggers and whatever else they had on their hands. Combined with shoddy logistics, poor morale, regional infighting and the Dunmers capacity to wage a liberation war, the First Alaqan Khaganate couldnt keep itself together under extreme external stress.

When the Second Fracturing occurred in 1299, the Dunmer realms once again took their chance at victories over the humans and waged bloody war against the Alaqans, succeeding in gaining more territory. House Hlagir and House Krig fought over who would keep Ulganmoor, a mid sized city with both access to the Iccin River and solid positioning on land trade routes across East Shamat. With mediation from House Segvu, it was decided to keep it as a free, independent city state that would act as a buffer between Alaqar and the Dunmer. House Hlagir, House Krig and those in charge of Ulganmoor, at the time an elected council, all agreed to this deal, and Ulganmoor was created as a free state in 1314 in the midst of brutal conflict and strife. Ulganmoor prospered under these conditions, continuing to hold steady trade routes through East Shamat despite the constant fighting in both Alaqar and the Dunmer lands and overall becoming a stable stronghold of Dunmer community and culture.

Cities like Knamaxid and Ulganmoor went through major economic and cultural reforms during this time. Dunmer exploits in the collapsing Alaqan Khaganate brought fame and attention to the region, and trade increased dramatically for the Dunmer kingdoms. However, a cultural shift had also began between the Dunmer kingdoms, particularly between the north and south. As the northern and southern kingdoms grew, their mild differences and cultural background became much more pronounced, namely in their way of life. Ulganmoor, Hlagirhan, Segvuvid, and Kriglives were all southern kingdoms which followed a more agricultural system of life, growing yams, wheat, rice, and their famed fungal plants for either self sustainability or for export as produce. The northern kingdoms, however, were built off of mining, smithing, and overall city based work due to the rougher soil and hard rock that made up much of the geography. This led to a cultural divide that caused problems in future attempts at a united Dunmer state, as trying to appeal to the populations of northern Dunmer and southern Dunmer proved difficult.

In 1429, the First Alaqan Khaganate finally collapsed into numerous kingdoms, khanates and city states. The Dunmer had by now conquered through the Shaki Mountains and down south of Alaqar, establishing a presence south of Angjus and Terakhia. Interestingly, the century post-Final Fracturing saw the most contact and coexistence between Dunmer and human populations up to that point. Alaqan kingdoms such as Nasiv and Yalakol worked with Dunmer kingdoms and wealthy Houses to support each other against their respective enemies. This came to be very beneficial for both populations, as Alaqar saw Dunmer populations migrate west looking for jobs in blacksmithing, farming or construction. The Dunmer realms, on the other hand, saw Alaqans migrate to their realms to escape poverty, serve as military troops or work agricultural jobs. When Alaqar reunited in the Wars of Reunification, the Dunmer and human relationship had improved considerably and building diplomatic relations was less difficult than beforehand.

Segvuvid and Hlagirhan both sent troops, food and money to the Second Alaqan Khaganate when the Holy Hydronic Empire invaded in 1544. Kriglives was in a bloody civil war at this time and struggled to find leftover funds for foreign support, and Ulganmoor remained loyal to their neutral ideals and didnt send support to either side. Alaqar managed to defend themselves from the Holy Hydronic invasion with Dunmer help. In 1616, the Dunmer realms experienced a wave of republican ideals that sparked internal divisions, conflict and threats of revolution. The old order of House and family dominated governance was challenged by new democratic ideals and principles both from abroad and from both Alaqar and the Dunmer homelands. Influential leaders of this movement include Gadro Rolsen, who publicly advocated for the establishment of a parliament, Bolydil Nulam, who led a rag-tag rebel group to set fire to a Segvuvid royal mushroom and Elohan Nasydram, who made speeches preaching the works of Elseyran and Vespurian republicans abroad. Ultimately, it had mixed results for the Dunmer kingdoms. Segvuvid was hit heavily by the revolution and implemented an elected parliament to advise those in House Segvu. Kriglives and Hlagirhan were able to resist the revolutionary ideals to an extent and preserve their Houses powers in government. Ulganmoor embraced the concepts, as it was already led by an elected council of 13 members and featured a democratic constitution. Alaqar next door broke under the revolutionary strain and was forced to implement a parliament into their monarchical system.

In September of 1831, an active volcano known as Ivohnid went through an incredibly destructive eruption. Located in northern Hlagirhan, the volcano spewed ash, dust and hot rock into the atmosphere for months, plastering the sky above in a deep grey cloud. This constant spew of ash into the sky sprayed dust and rock that covered hundreds of thousands of square miles throughout the Dunmer kingdoms. This proved to be fatal for the Dunmer inhabitants, bringing famine, civil turmoil and disease to the region. Dunmer people were suddenly leaving their homeland in droves in search of jobs, food or to escape from poverty. This led to the biggest contributor to Dunmer diaspora populations in the modern day, as Dunmer stayed strong to their identity even after leaving their native communities. This cataclysmic eruption would also spell the end for the regions native Dunmer kingdoms. The Second Alaqan Khaganate to the north had recently signed a peace treaty with the crumbling Holy Hydronic Empire, which had just lost the Final War against Alaqar and the Kingdom of Bob. When the Holy Hydronic Empire dissolved into the Democratic Republic of United Hydronia, Alaqar seized an opportunity to spread their influence in East Shamat while Hydronia was recovering.

Food, money, water, and other supplies were sold to the Dunmer kingdoms down south. Alaqar staged this as an act of good will, to support their Dunmer brothers in trying times. However, this quickly turned out to be a sham, as Alaqan officials sold goods and supplies at inflated prices that took bites out of the Dunmer economy. Combined with Alaqan diplomatic pressure and a worsening financial home situation for the Dunmer at home, Kriglives became a protectorate of the Second Alaqan Khaganate in 1836 and was folded into the Khaganate 4 years later. Hlagirhan was turned into a vassal in 1838 and annexed into Alaqar in 1841. Segvuvid resisted Alaqan attempts at annexation for several years, and only joined in 1850 after Alaqar signed several bills into place protecting the rights of Dunmer in the Khaganate. Ulganmoor joined the Alaqan Khaganate on their own accord in 1841 shortly after Hlagirhan was annexed to avoid sparking conflict with its larger neighbor.
